# EnumerableWithCountSizeReference Review

Source: https://github.com/jkamsker/fourser.gen/blob/main/docs/tasks/review-output/EnumerableWithCountSizeReference.md

# EnumerableWithCountSizeReference Review

## Verdict
Not acceptable as the current golden output. The checked-in `verified.txt` is no longer the generator's actual output, and even on its own terms it only behaves safely for replayable `IEnumerable<Entity>` sources.

## Findings
1. High: The checked-in snapshot is stale relative to the current generator output. A targeted `RunGeneratorTest` for this case now fails because the generator no longer emits the count-backfill/seek-based serialization shown in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerableWithCountSizeReference/EnumerableWithCountSizeReference.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:91-106` and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerableWithCountSizeReference/EnumerableWithCountSizeReference.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:120-142`. That makes this file a poor representation of current behavior and unlikely to match user expectations for the test case.
2. Medium: The verified implementation assumes `MyList` can be enumerated repeatedly. `GetPacketSize` first materializes and walks `obj.MyList` in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerableWithCountSizeReference/EnumerableWithCountSizeReference.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:29-39`, then both serialize overloads enumerate `obj.MyList` again in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerableWithCountSizeReference/EnumerableWithCountSizeReference.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:94-106` and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerableWithCountSizeReference/EnumerableWithCountSizeReference.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:127-142`. For deferred or single-use sequences, that can produce size/count mismatches or serialization failures, which is hard to square with advertising `IEnumerable<T>` support in `README.md:513-520` and with the property type in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerableWithCountSizeReference/input.cs:11-12`.
3. Medium: `Serialize(Stream)` needlessly rejects non-seekable streams in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerableWithCountSizeReference/EnumerableWithCountSizeReference.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:120-123`. For a count-prefixed collection this is a user-visible limitation, especially for network and pipe streams, and it is avoidable by preparing the enumerable before writing.

## Performance Opportunities
- `GetPacketSize` allocates an array solely to iterate it once in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerableWithCountSizeReference/EnumerableWithCountSizeReference.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:29-39`. That buffering is redundant in this snapshot because serialization still re-enumerates the original sequence instead of reusing the prepared data.
- Both serialize overloads could add `ICollection<T>` / `IReadOnlyCollection<T>` fast paths before falling back to prepared-sequence handling. The current verified code always uses placeholder bookkeeping in span mode and stream rewinds in stream mode (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerableWithCountSizeReference/EnumerableWithCountSizeReference.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:91-106`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerableWithCountSizeReference/EnumerableWithCountSizeReference.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:124-142`), even when the runtime object may already expose a cheap `Count`.
- The stream path performs extra I/O repositioning with `stream.Position` rewrites in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerableWithCountSizeReference/EnumerableWithCountSizeReference.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:139-142`. Writing the count once up front after preparing the sequence would reduce that overhead and remove the seek requirement.

## Open Questions / Assumptions
- Assumed `CountSizeReference` is meant to serialize the actual collection length rather than preserve the incoming `Count` property value. That matches the documented contract in `README.md:181-190`.
- Did not treat the duplicated `using` blocks for `EnumerableOfReferenceTypes` and `Entity` as a material issue, because Verify concatenates multiple generated files into one snapshot.

# EnumerationTypes Review

Source: https://github.com/jkamsker/fourser.gen/blob/main/docs/tasks/review-output/EnumerationTypes.md

# EnumerationTypes Review

## Verdict
Not fully correct. Most of the generated code looks reasonable, but the `IEnumerable<byte>` member is unsafe for single-pass/stateful enumerables, so I would not treat this verified output as fully functionally correct or fully aligned with likely user expectations.

## Findings
- High: `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerationTypes/input.cs:14-16` declares `Data` as `IEnumerable<byte>`, but `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerationTypes/EnumerationTypes.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:38-40` materializes it during `GetPacketSize`, and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerationTypes/EnumerationTypes.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:441-455` plus `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerationTypes/EnumerationTypes.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:682-696` can enumerate/materialize it again during serialization. In the normal `new byte[T.GetPacketSize(obj)]` then `T.Serialize(obj, buffer)` flow, a single-pass enumerable can throw on the second enumeration or produce different bytes than the size calculation assumed. That makes the output functionally unsafe for the shape under test and does not match likely expectations for enumerable support. Supporting intent already exists elsewhere: `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTests.cs:430-451` names this scenario `CountedByteEnumerableSerialization_ShouldMaterializeAtMostOnce`, and `tests/FourSer.Tests.Behavioural/UseCases/CollectionGenerationRegressionTests.cs:93-125` already protects one-pass enumerable sizing in a related case.
- Low: `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerationTypes/EnumerationTypes.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:4`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerationTypes/EnumerationTypes.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:7-10`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerationTypes/EnumerationTypes.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:39-40`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerationTypes/EnumerationTypes.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:140-147`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerationTypes/EnumerationTypes.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:282-289`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerationTypes/EnumerationTypes.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:529-531`, and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerationTypes/EnumerationTypes.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:769-772` contain avoidable redundancy: unused `using`s, `dataSizedItems?.Count()` instead of `dataSizedItems.Length`, and repeated `AsSpan()`/`CollectionsMarshal.AsSpan(...)` lookups inside loops. This is not a correctness problem, but it is duplicate noise in generated output.

## Performance opportunities
- Reuse a single materialization of `Data` across sizing and serialization, or emit a reserved-count single-pass writer for pure `IEnumerable<byte>` sources. The current code allocates during sizing and may allocate again during serialization.
- Hoist `AsSpan()`/`CollectionsMarshal.AsSpan(...)` results into locals before hot loops for `Numbers` and `ArrayData` to avoid repeated span construction.
- Consider runtime fast paths for interface-typed primitive collections when the runtime value is actually a `List<T>` or array. `Measurements` is emitted as per-element writes in both span and stream paths (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerationTypes/EnumerationTypes.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:541-544` and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/EnumerationTypes/EnumerationTypes.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:782-785`), which misses a possible block-write optimization.

## Open questions / assumptions
- Assumed the expected contract is that `GetPacketSize(obj)` followed by `Serialize(obj, ...)` works for single-pass as well as replayable `IEnumerable<byte>` sources, because that is the library's standard usage pattern in behavioural tests and benchmark helpers.
- Assumed unordered collections such as `ConcurrentBag<T>` and `HashSet<T>` only need correct round-trip membership, not deterministic wire ordering. I did not treat their native iteration-order serialization as a defect here.
- Other than the `IEnumerable<byte>` path, I did not find additional material functional issues in this test case.

# ListOfStructs Review

Source: https://github.com/jkamsker/fourser.gen/blob/main/docs/tasks/review-output/ListOfStructs.md

# ListOfStructs Review

## Verdict
Functionally correct for the modeled `List<MyStruct>` round-trip in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/ListOfStructs/input.cs`. I did not find a material correctness bug in the emitted serializer. The main gap is that the generated code does not match likely user expectations for the generator's default optimization mode, because this trivially fixed-size struct list still falls back to per-element work instead of a bulk path.

## Findings
### Medium - Default-mode collection fast path is missed for a trivially fixed-size struct list
- `MyStruct` is only a single `int` field in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/ListOfStructs/input.cs:3-6`, and the generated serializer confirms each element is always 4 bytes and encoded as one `Int32` in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/ListOfStructs/ListOfStructs.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:21-68`.
- Even so, the list serializer still sizes the collection item-by-item in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/ListOfStructs/ListOfStructs.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:99-105`, deserializes item-by-item in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/ListOfStructs/ListOfStructs.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:121-146`, and serializes item-by-item in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/ListOfStructs/ListOfStructs.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:164-193`.
- That is surprising under the default `AggressivePortable` mode, because collection fast paths are enabled by default in `src/FourSer.Gen/FourSerGeneratorOptions.cs:18-24` and `src/FourSer.Gen/FourSerGeneratorOptions.cs:44-45`. The current optimizer explicitly excludes collection elements that also have `[GenerateSerializer]` in `src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/Optimization/CollectionFastPathPass.cs:132-137`, so `List<MyStruct>` misses batching even though this specific generated serializer is layout-trivial.

### Low - Redundant generated boilerplate is repeated for both emitted types
- The full prologue/import block is emitted once for `MyStruct` and then repeated for `PacketWithListOfStructs` in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/ListOfStructs/ListOfStructs.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:1-15` and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/ListOfStructs/ListOfStructs.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:72-86`.
- This is harmless at runtime, but it is redundant source bloat and makes the verified output harder to review than necessary.

## Performance opportunities
- Batch `Structs` span/stream reads and writes as contiguous bytes when a generated struct serializer is provably fixed-size and little-endian compatible. In this case that would replace the per-item calls in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/ListOfStructs/ListOfStructs.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:121-146` and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/ListOfStructs/ListOfStructs.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:164-193` with one count prefix plus one bulk copy/read over the list span.
- Fold packet sizing from the per-item loop in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/ListOfStructs/ListOfStructs.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:99-105` to `sizeof(int) + obj.Structs.Count * 4`, since `MyStruct.GetPacketSize(...)` is constant `4` in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/ListOfStructs/ListOfStructs.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:21-25`.
- Cache `checked((int)structsCount)` once during deserialization instead of repeating it in both the list-capacity expression and loop condition at `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/ListOfStructs/ListOfStructs.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:123-124` and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/ListOfStructs/ListOfStructs.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:142-143`.

## Open questions / assumptions
- I assumed collapsing `null` and empty collections is intentional here. `Serialize` writes count `0` for `null` at `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/ListOfStructs/ListOfStructs.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:158-160` and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/ListOfStructs/ListOfStructs.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:183-185`, while deserialize always materializes a new list at `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/ListOfStructs/ListOfStructs.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:123-129` and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/ListOfStructs/ListOfStructs.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:142-148`. That matches other collection fixtures in this repo, so I did not score it as a defect for this case.
- I could not run the filtered `FourSer.Tests` cases locally because the machine is missing `Microsoft.NETCore.App` `9.0.0`; the review is otherwise based on source inspection and generator behavior.

# MemoryOwner Review

Source: https://github.com/jkamsker/fourser.gen/blob/main/docs/tasks/review-output/MemoryOwner.md

# MemoryOwner Review

## Verdict

Not correct as generated. The `IMemoryOwner<T>` fast paths are mostly sound and already use bulk reads and writes, but `Parent.DisposableProperty` is declared nullable and emitted as mandatory, and `Parent.Deserialize` can leak the rented `Data` owner when nested deserialization fails.

## Findings

1. High: `Child? DisposableProperty` cannot round-trip `null`.
   - `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/input.cs:15` declares the property nullable.
   - The generated size and serialize paths throw if it is null in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:164`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:166`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:249`, and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:277`.
   - The deserialize path always reads a `Child` directly, with no null marker or alternate null case, in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:201` and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:228`.
   - Result: the generated wire format cannot represent one of the declared input states, which is both a functional mismatch and unlikely user expectation for `Child?`.

2. Medium: `Parent.Deserialize` leaks the rented `Data` owner when `Child.Deserialize` fails.
   - `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:189` to `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:200` and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:216` to `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:227` dispose `dataOwner` only while filling the owner itself.
   - After ownership is assigned to `data`, the next nested read in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:201` and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:228` can still throw, at which point the already-rented `IMemoryOwner<byte>` is lost and never disposed.
   - This matters on truncated or corrupt payloads and on any nested deserializer exception.

3. Low: The generated output contains redundant boilerplate.
   - The same auto-generated banner and using block are emitted twice for the two types in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:1` to `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:15` and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:137` to `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:151`.
   - Several imports in those blocks are unused in this case, including `System.Buffers.Binary`, `System.Collections.Generic`, `System.Linq`, `System.Runtime.CompilerServices`, and `System.Text`.

## Performance opportunities

- Zero-count deserialization still rents from `MemoryPool<T>` and may allocate a `MemoryOwnerWrapper<T>` through `SliceToSize(0)` in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:46`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:72`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:189`, and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:216`, with the wrapper created by `src/FourSer.Gen/Resources/Code/MemoryPoolExtensions.cs:8` to `src/FourSer.Gen/Resources/Code/MemoryPoolExtensions.cs:20`. A cached empty owner would avoid pool traffic and wrapper allocation for the null and empty case.
- The payload paths already use bulk `ReadBytes`, `ReadExactly`, and `WriteBytes` for `byte` and unmanaged `int` memory owners in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:50`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:76`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:103`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:126`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:193`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:220`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:247`, and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/MemoryOwner/MemoryOwner.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:275`. The remaining batching opportunity is small: fuse the count-prefix write with the immediate payload write to cut a few tiny stream calls.

## Open questions / assumptions

- I treated nullable `IMemoryOwner<T>` canonicalization (`null` to a zero-length owner) as intentional, not a bug, because `tests/FourSer.Tests/OptimizationCollectionFailureTests.cs:101` to `tests/FourSer.Tests/OptimizationCollectionFailureTests.cs:145` explicitly asserts that behavior.
- I assumed nullable reference annotations should matter for nested generated types as well. The current planning and emission code always throws on null nested references and never emits a null marker in `src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/Planning/SerializePlanBuilder.cs:194` to `src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/Planning/SerializePlanBuilder.cs:203`, `src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/Planning/SizePlanBuilder.cs:24` to `src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/Planning/SizePlanBuilder.cs:40`, `src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/Emission/PlanTypeEmitter.cs:34` to `src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/Emission/PlanTypeEmitter.cs:51`, and `src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/Planning/DeserializePlanBuilder.cs:123` to `src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/Planning/DeserializePlanBuilder.cs:132`.
- I could not execute the targeted `FourSer.Tests` cases locally because the installed runtimes are `Microsoft.NETCore.App` `8.0.26` and `10.0.6`, while the test host for this repo requires `9.0.0`.

# NestedObject Review

Source: https://github.com/jkamsker/fourser.gen/blob/main/docs/tasks/review-output/NestedObject.md

# NestedObject Review

## Verdict
Functionally correct and aligned with likely user expectations for this fixture. The generated code matches the shape of `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NestedObject/input.cs:3-15`, emits the expected single null guard for the nested member in each sizing/serialize method (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTests.cs:632-654`), and matches the current runtime contract that nested reference members are required during sizing/serialization (`tests/FourSer.Tests.Behavioural/Nested/NestedObjectsTests.cs:44-56`). No material functional findings.

## Findings
- Low: `NestedData.Serialize(Stream)` duplicates the UTF-8 length/payload write logic inline instead of reusing the shared helper. `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NestedObject/NestedObject.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:189-226` inlines the same basic algorithm as `src/FourSer.Gen/Resources/Code/StreamWriterHelpers.cs:120-155`, and that code is emitted from `src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/Emission/PlanScalarEmitter.cs:75-123`. This is functionally correct and likely intentional for the fused single-write path, but it is still redundant generated code that can drift from the helper over time.

## Performance opportunities
- No additional scalar batching looks available inside `ContainerPacket` itself. The only fixed-size member before the nested object is `Id` (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NestedObject/NestedObject.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:78`, `:97`), which is only 4 bytes, below the default 8-byte batching threshold in `src/FourSer.Gen/FourSerGeneratorOptions.cs:18-24` and `src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/Core/BatchingUtilities.cs:16`. The nested member is also intentionally excluded from batching because generated nested serializers may be variable-sized (`src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/Core/BatchingUtilities.cs:118-120`).
- `NestedData.Serialize(Stream)` could reduce stream IO further by extending the already-fused string buffer to append the trailing `float Value`, then issuing one `stream.Write(...)` for the whole nested payload instead of the current fused string write plus `StreamWriter.WriteSingle(...)` (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NestedObject/NestedObject.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:201-226`).
- The fused inline string path uses the generator `StackallocThreshold` of 256 total bytes (`src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/Emission/PlanScalarEmitter.cs:83-96`, `src/FourSer.Gen/FourSerGeneratorOptions.cs:18-24`), while `StreamWriterHelpers.WriteString` keeps string payloads on the stack up to 512 bytes (`src/FourSer.Gen/Resources/Code/StreamWriterHelpers.cs:136-153`). Unifying those thresholds, or centralizing the implementation, would reduce code size and may avoid unnecessary `ArrayPool<byte>` rent/return traffic for mid-sized strings.

## Open questions / assumptions
- I assumed the FourSer string contract intentionally canonicalizes `null` and `string.Empty` to the same wire representation. `NestedData.Name` therefore behaves consistently with the rest of the runtime, even though `null` would deserialize back as `string.Empty`.
- I could not execute the filtered `dotnet test` runs end-to-end on this machine because the projects target `net9.0` and the local runtime is missing `Microsoft.NETCore.App 9.0.0`. The assessment is therefore based on source review, successful project build during `dotnet test`, and the existing generator/behavioral test coverage cited above.

# NullCollectionDynamicCount Review

## Verdict
Not functionally correct for the null-collection scenario, and likely not what a user expects from a fixture named `NullCollectionDynamicCount`. The generated code does honor `[SerializeCollection(CountType = typeof(byte))]` for non-null lists, but it serializes `null` as a zero count and always deserializes zero back to `new List<Item>(0)`, so `Items == null` does not round-trip.

## Findings ordered by severity

The generator logic is consistent with that lossy encoding at [CollectionSerializer.cs#L264](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/Logic/CollectionSerializer.cs#L264) and [CollectionSerializer.cs#L267](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/Logic/CollectionSerializer.cs#L267), but that is exactly why this fixture looks expectation-mismatched.
- Low: `GetPacketSize` does avoidable per-item overflow counting even though `List<T>` already exposes `Count`. The generated loop increments `itemsValidatedCount` on every element at [NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L117](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionDynamicCount/NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L117) and [NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L120](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionDynamicCount/NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L120). The current packet-size generator already has a cheaper direct-count validation path for count-bearing collections at [PacketSizeGenerator.cs#L186](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/PacketSizeGenerator.cs#L186), [PacketSizeGenerator.cs#L190](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/PacketSizeGenerator.cs#L190), and [PacketSizeGenerator.cs#L214](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/PacketSizeGenerator.cs#L214), so the emitted loop work is redundant for this `List<Item>` shape.
- Info: the verified snapshot contains repeated boilerplate and some local-variable noise. The second `// <auto-generated/>` plus duplicate `using`/alias block at [NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L87](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionDynamicCount/NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L87) through [NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L101](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionDynamicCount/NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L101) is snapshot concatenation from [GeneratorTests.cs#L78](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTests.cs#L78) through [GeneratorTests.cs#L83](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTests.cs#L83), not a compilation issue. Separately, both deserializers carry unnecessary `itemsValue -> items` handoff locals and repeat `checked((int)itemsCount)` at [NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L144](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionDynamicCount/NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L144), [NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L145](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionDynamicCount/NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L145), [NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L149](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionDynamicCount/NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L149), [NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L163](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionDynamicCount/NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L163), [NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L164](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionDynamicCount/NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L164), and [NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L168](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionDynamicCount/NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L168).

## Performance opportunities
- Deserialize the pre-sized `List<Item>` without repeated `Add(...)` calls. The current loops at [NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L145](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionDynamicCount/NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L145), [NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L147](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionDynamicCount/NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L147), [NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L164](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionDynamicCount/NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L164), and [NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L166](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionDynamicCount/NullCollectionDynamicCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt#L166) could use `CollectionsMarshal.SetCount(...)` plus span-slot assignment, matching the existing optimized emitter shape at [PlannedCollectionReadEmitter.cs#L117](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/Emission/PlannedCollectionReadEmitter.cs#L117) through [PlannedCollectionReadEmitter.cs#L124](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/Emission/PlannedCollectionReadEmitter.cs#L124).

There is no broad collection fast path here, though, because `Item` is a generated-serializer reference type rather than a contiguous unmanaged element type.

## Open questions / assumptions
- Assumed the fixture name is intentional and that preserving a meaningful distinction between `null` and empty collections matters more here than merely honoring the `byte` count width.
- If the intended contract is "count-prefixed nullable collections are canonicalized to empty on deserialize," then the top issue is an expectation mismatch rather than a generator bug. That intent is at least hinted at by the zero-fallback comments in [GeneratorUtilities.cs#L53](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/Core/GeneratorUtilities.cs#L53) through [GeneratorUtilities.cs#L69](C:/Users/Jonas/repos/private/JKamsker/FourSer.Gen/src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/Core/GeneratorUtilities.cs#L69).
- I did not run the generator or behavioural tests for this review; conclusions are based on static inspection of the fixture, generated snapshot, and the relevant generator paths.

# NullCollectionStaticCount Review

Source: https://github.com/jkamsker/fourser.gen/blob/main/docs/tasks/review-output/NullCollectionStaticCount.md

# NullCollectionStaticCount Review

## Verdict
Functionally correct for FourSer's current collection contract. The generated code accepts a `null` `Items` collection, encodes it as count `0`, and deserializes zero-count payloads to an empty `List<Item>` (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:115`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:177`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:141`). That matches the current collection behavior covered elsewhere in the test suite (`tests/FourSer.Tests.Behavioural/Collections/CollectionTests.cs:97-109`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/OptimizationCollectionFailureTests.cs:101-145`). The static-count part is also correct: sizing reserves one fixed `int` count prefix and does not introduce extra validation bookkeeping (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:114`).

The main expectation caveat is that `Items` is declared non-nullable in a nullable-enabled project (`Directory.Build.props:5`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/input.cs:16`), but the generated code still treats it as optional.

## Findings
1. Low: The generated serializer ignores the source nullability contract for `Items`. `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/input.cs:16` declares `List<Item> Items` in a nullable-enabled project, but the generated code accepts `null` in sizing and serialization (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:115-125`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:177-180`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:206-209`) and always materializes a non-null `List<Item>` on deserialize (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:141-149`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:159-168`). This matches current collection handling for nullable lists (`tests/FourSer.Tests.Behavioural/Collections/CollectionTests.cs:97-109`) and the generator's `List<T>` metadata (`src/FourSer.Gen/TypeInfoProvider.cs:239-250`), so it is not a functional regression, but it is likely surprising for users who read the member as required.
2. Info: The verification artifact contains duplicate `// <auto-generated/>` banners and repeated `using` / alias blocks at `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:1-15` and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:87-101`. `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTests.cs:78-83` concatenates multiple generated `*.g.cs` files into one snapshot, so this is snapshot noise rather than a functional issue in a single emitted source file.
3. Info: Both deserializers include redundant `checked((int)itemsCount)` casts and extra one-shot temporaries in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:141-149` and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:159-168`. `itemsCount` is already an `int`, so those casts do not add overflow protection for this case.

## Performance opportunities
- Stream collection IO is still per-element. `MainObject.Deserialize(stream)` and `Serialize(obj, stream)` delegate once per item (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:164`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:219`), and each `Item` stream method reduces to a single 4-byte primitive read/write (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:57`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:82`). Because `Item` is fixed-width (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:27-29`), a future buffered collection path could reduce O(n) tiny stream operations to one bulk read/write plus in-memory processing.
- Collection sizing and serialization duplicate element null guards before calling `Item.GetPacketSize` / `Item.Serialize`, and those delegated methods immediately perform their own root-null guards again (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:119-123` with `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:21-29`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:186-190` with `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:62-69`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:215-219` with `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/NullCollectionStaticCount.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:76-82`). An internal trusted-non-null path could remove one branch per element.
- No major span batching gap is apparent beyond that. `Item` is a reference type, so the unmanaged `CollectionsMarshal` bulk path used for primitive lists does not apply directly here.

## Open questions / assumptions
- Assuming this case is meant to validate the current "null collection serializes as zero count and round-trips as empty" behavior, the snapshot is correct.
- If the intent was to honor the source nullability contract in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullCollectionStaticCount/input.cs:16`, this test case should probably either declare `Items` as `List<Item>?` or use an explicit null-preserving encoding mode that distinguishes `null` from empty.

# NullProperty Review

# NullProperty Review

## Verdict
Functionally correct for `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullProperty/input.cs` and aligned with likely user expectations for this repo. `MainObject.Nested` is declared non-nullable in a nullable-enabled project (`Directory.Build.props:5`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullProperty/input.cs:15`), and the generated code consistently rejects `null` during sizing and serialization while always materializing a nested instance during deserialization (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullProperty/NullProperty.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:107`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullProperty/NullProperty.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:131`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullProperty/NullProperty.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:152`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullProperty/NullProperty.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:170`). That also matches the current nested-object behavioral contract, which throws on `null` nested references (`tests/FourSer.Tests.Behavioural/Nested/NestedObjectsTests.cs:44`, `tests/FourSer.Tests.Behavioural/Nested/NestedObjectsTests.cs:52`).

## Findings
No material correctness or expectation findings.

1. Info: The verification snapshot contains duplicate `// <auto-generated/>` banners and repeated `using` / alias blocks at `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullProperty/NullProperty.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:1` and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullProperty/NullProperty.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:87`. This is snapshot noise from concatenating multiple generated `*.g.cs` files in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTests.cs:78` and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTests.cs:83`, not a functional issue in the generated code itself.

The deserializers also use one-shot temporaries before returning in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullProperty/NullProperty.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:133`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullProperty/NullProperty.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:135`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullProperty/NullProperty.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:146`, and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullProperty/NullProperty.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:148`.

## Performance opportunities
- No meaningful batching or stream/IO reduction opportunity is missing here. The nested payload is a single `int`, so the hot path already boils down to one primitive read or write in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullProperty/NullProperty.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:57`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullProperty/NullProperty.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:68`, and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/NullProperty/NullProperty.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:82`.
- Only micro-optimizations are apparent: the generator could inline the trivial nested serializer/size logic into `MainObject` to remove one method call and the duplicated null checks noted above, but that would not change the number of stream operations.

## Open questions / assumptions
- Assuming the intended contract for nested reference members is "required unless FourSer adds an explicit nullable encoding mode," this case is correct and the generated output matches current behavior.
- A targeted `dotnet test 'tests/FourSer.Tests/FourSer.Tests.csproj' --filter "DisplayName~NullProperty"` was attempted, but this environment cannot run the `net9.0` test host because `Microsoft.NETCore.App 9.0.0` is not installed. The verdict is therefore based on source inspection plus the existing behavioral nested-object tests.

# PolymorphicCollectionIEnumerable Review

Source: https://github.com/jkamsker/fourser.gen/blob/main/docs/tasks/review-output/PolymorphicCollectionIEnumerable.md

# PolymorphicCollectionIEnumerable Review

## Verdict
Mostly correct for round-tripping homogeneous `IEnumerable<Item>` values on span and seekable-stream paths, but not fully aligned with likely user expectations. The main issue is that the generated `Serialize(Stream)` path unnecessarily requires a seekable stream even though the enumerable is eagerly buffered first; there is also a lower-severity surprise around nullability and implicit default-discriminator handling for empty or `null` collections.

## Findings
1. Medium: `Serialize(Stream)` is more restrictive than necessary and will fail on non-seekable writable streams. `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionIEnumerable/PolymorphicCollectionIEnumerable.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:273-325` eagerly materializes `obj.Items` into `itemsValidatedItems = Enumerable.ToList(obj.Items)`, so the item count is already known before any bytes are written. Despite that, `:312-317` still enforces `stream.CanSeek`, writes a placeholder count, and later seeks back to patch it at `:373-376`. For this `IEnumerable<Item>` case the generated stream serializer could write `itemsValidatedItems.Count` up front and stream directly to sockets, pipes, and other non-seekable streams. That restriction is not implied by `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionIEnumerable/input.cs:9-13`, so it is a likely behavior gap for users.
2. Low: The non-nullable `Items` member is still treated as optional, and empty or `null` values silently use the first polymorphic option as the discriminator. `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionIEnumerable/input.cs:9-13` declares `IEnumerable<Item> Items` without `?` and without an explicit default `[PolymorphicOption(..., isDefault: true)]`, but the generated serializer accepts `null` and empty collections, writing type id `10` at `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionIEnumerable/PolymorphicCollectionIEnumerable.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:200-203`, `:210-223`, `:318-320`, and `:327-339`, then always deserializes to a non-null `List<Item>` at `:68-70`, `:103-104`, `:114-116`, and `:149-150`. That fallback is internally consistent with `src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/Core/PolymorphicUtilities.cs:9-38`, which uses `options[0]` when no explicit default is marked, but it is still likely surprising from the source model alone.
3. Info: The snapshot contains substantial duplicate generated logic and noise. The span and stream serializers repeat the same first-item discriminator resolution and per-item validation logic almost verbatim at `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionIEnumerable/PolymorphicCollectionIEnumerable.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:159-196` and `:273-310`, then recompute the discriminator again for the write switch at `:216-256` and `:332-372`. The concatenated snapshot also repeats identical prologue blocks and nearly identical zero-member serializers for `Item`, `Sword`, `Shield`, and `Potion` at `:383-676`. This is not a correctness issue, but it is redundant generated code.

## Performance opportunities
- Since `itemsValidatedItems` is already a `List<Item>` in both serializers at `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionIEnumerable/PolymorphicCollectionIEnumerable.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:159` and `:273`, write `itemsValidatedItems.Count` directly instead of reserving and backpatching the count. On the stream path that would also remove the `CanSeek` requirement, two position changes, and one extra count write.
- Reuse the validated discriminator from the prepass instead of recomputing it from `itemsEnumerator.Current` in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionIEnumerable/PolymorphicCollectionIEnumerable.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:216-223` and `:332-339`.
- Replace `itemsValidatedItems?.Count() ?? 0` in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionIEnumerable/PolymorphicCollectionIEnumerable.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:160` and `:274` with the list's `Count` property to avoid needless LINQ dispatch.
- `GetPacketSize` materializes the enumerable to an array and walks it at `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionIEnumerable/PolymorphicCollectionIEnumerable.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:29-53`, while `Serialize` materializes it to a list and revalidates or walks it again at `:159-257` and `:273-378`. That is mostly an API-shape cost for pure `IEnumerable<T>` members, but it is the main remaining allocation and CPU overhead in this case.

## Open questions / assumptions
- Assuming current intended behavior is that `SingleTypeId` collections without an explicit default discriminator fall back to the first declared `[PolymorphicOption]`, the empty and `null` encoding here is internally consistent.
- Assuming the library wants `Serialize(Stream)` to work on any writable stream when the count is already known in memory, the seekability check above is a real behavior gap rather than just an optimization miss.
- This review is based on source inspection only. I did not run generator or behavioral tests because the task restricted writes to the report file.

---

# PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray Review

Source: https://github.com/jkamsker/fourser.gen/blob/main/docs/tasks/review-output/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.md

# PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray Review

## Verdict
Functionally correct for `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/input.cs` and aligned with likely user expectations for an `ImmutableArray<IItem>` using `PolymorphicMode.IndividualTypeIds`. The generated code writes a count plus a per-item byte discriminator, preserves item order on deserialize, materializes `ImmutableArray<IItem>` again, and correctly supports mixed `Sword` / `Shield` / `Potion` items (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/input.cs:8-12`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:28-38`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:55-83`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:141-170`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:193-223`). No material correctness or expectation mismatches found.

## Findings
1. Low: Both serialize paths perform a full pre-validation pass over `Items` before the real write loop, but the subsequent polymorphic `switch` already contains `case null` / `default` guards. That duplicates iteration and null-checking work without changing behavior (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:134-145`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:166-169`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:186-197`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:218-221`).
2. Info: The `Sword`, `Shield`, and `Potion` serializers are structurally identical zero-member boilerplate, and each repeats its own `using` / alias block. This is redundant generated code and increases snapshot/code size without adding behavior (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:229-300`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:303-374`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:377-448`).
3. Info: The same polymorphic type map is re-emitted across packet sizing, both deserializers, and both serializers. That is not a correctness issue, but it is repetitive generated code (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:38`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:61-79`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:101-119`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:146-169`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:198-221`).

## Performance opportunities
- Deserialize directly into an `ImmutableArray<IItem>` builder or other fixed-size backing store instead of `List<IItem>` + `ImmutableArray.CreateRange(...)`, which currently adds a staging collection and a second copy (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:55-83`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:95-123`).
- The stream serializer currently does one `StreamWriter.WriteByte` call per element, even though the leaf payload serializers are empty in this case. Batching the discriminator bytes would materially reduce stream calls for large collections (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:200-215`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:247-299`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:321-373`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:395-447`).
- If the generator keeps separate validation, combining type/null validation with packet-size calculation or the actual write pass would remove an extra full traversal over the immutable array (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:29-39`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:134-171`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:186-223`).

## Open questions / assumptions
- Assuming the current contract intentionally treats `ImmutableArray<T>.Default` the same as `ImmutableArray<T>.Empty` on the wire, this case is correct. The source member is non-nullable and initialized to `ImmutableArray<IItem>.Empty` (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/input.cs:12`), while the generated size/serialize paths use `IsDefaultOrEmpty` (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:29`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:141-142`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableArray.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:193-194`).
- A targeted `dotnet test` run could not execute locally because `Microsoft.NETCore.App 9.0.0` is not installed, so the verdict is based on static inspection of the verified output and the generator/test harness rather than a completed local test run.

# PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue Review

Source: https://github.com/jkamsker/fourser.gen/blob/main/docs/tasks/review-output/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.md

# PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue Review

## Verdict
Partially correct. The generated code should round-trip homogeneous `ImmutableQueue<IItem>` contents and preserve queue order, but it is not fully aligned with the declared `TypeIdProperty` contract or likely user expectations. `Inventory.ItemType` is never consulted during serialization; instead the serializer derives the discriminator from `Items` and falls back to `10` for empty or `null` queues (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/input.cs:8-16`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:163-223`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:290-349`). That matches current checked-in tests, but it is surprising relative to the contract comments (`src/FourSer.Contracts/PolymorphicMode.cs:14`, `src/FourSer.Contracts/SerializeCollectionAttribute.cs:39`). No other material correctness issue stood out in the immutable-queue handling itself.

## Findings
1. Medium: `TypeIdProperty` is effectively ignored on serialize. The generated deserialize path reads the wire `itemType` and assigns `Inventory.ItemType` (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:56-59`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:66-105`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:114-153`), but both serialize paths ignore `obj.ItemType`; they materialize `Items`, infer the discriminator from the first item, and hard-code `10` when the queue is empty or `null` (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:163-223`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:290-349`). For example, `new Inventory { ItemType = 20, Items = ImmutableQueue<IItem>.Empty }` would serialize as type id `10` and round-trip back with `ItemType = 10`. Given `TypeIdProperty = nameof(ItemType)` in `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/input.cs:12` and the contract wording in `src/FourSer.Contracts/PolymorphicMode.cs:14` / `src/FourSer.Contracts/SerializeCollectionAttribute.cs:39`, this does not match likely user expectations, even though current tests explicitly codify the same behavior (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTests.cs:240-275`, `tests/FourSer.Tests.Behavioural/Polymorphism/PolymorphicCollectionParityTests.cs:350-410`, `tests/FourSer.Tests.Behavioural/UseCases/SingleTypeIdTests.cs:42-96`).
2. Low: Each serialize path re-traverses the same buffered list multiple times and repeats the same discriminator switch three times. After `ToList(obj.Items)` (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:163`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:290`), the code does a validation pass (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:164-200`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:291-327`), a separate first-item pass to write the type id (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:202-223`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:329-349`), and another first-item pass before the type-specific write switch (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:230-274`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:357-400`). This is duplicate generated code and unnecessary CPU work for data that has already been materialized.
3. Info: The `Sword`, `Shield`, and `Potion` serializers are identical zero-member boilerplate, and each repeats its own `using` / alias prologue (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:408-479`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:482-553`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:556-627`). That is not a behavior bug, but it is redundant generated output.

## Performance opportunities
- Cache `count` and validated `discriminator` from the first pass and reuse them instead of calling `Count()` and reopening enumerators later (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:163-231`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:290-358`). Because `itemsValidatedItems` is already a `List<IItem>`, use `.Count` instead of LINQ `.Count()` at `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:164`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:202`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:230-231`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:291`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:329`, and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:357-358`.
- There is no meaningful stream batching opportunity inside the item loop in this specific case because `Sword.Serialize(stream)`, `Shield.Serialize(stream)`, and `Potion.Serialize(stream)` are zero-byte no-ops (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:472-478`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:546-552`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:620-626`). The real wins here are reducing list traversals and duplicate discriminator work, not additional IO coalescing.
- If the generator can recognize zero-payload homogeneous leaf types, it could skip the per-item serialize loops entirely after validation because the switch cases at `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:248-269` and `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableQueue.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:375-396` currently do CPU work without emitting any item bytes.

## Open questions / assumptions
- Assuming the current project intentionally recomputes `SingleTypeId` from collection contents and uses the first declared `[PolymorphicOption]` when no explicit default is marked, this snapshot matches existing checked-in behavior even though it conflicts with the public contract comments.
- A local `dotnet test` verification could not be completed because the environment is missing `Microsoft.NETCore.App 9.0.0`; this review is based on static inspection plus the checked-in generator and behavioral tests that already assert the current `TypeIdProperty` semantics.

# PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack Review

Source: https://github.com/jkamsker/fourser.gen/blob/main/docs/tasks/review-output/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack.md

# PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack Review

## Verdict
Functionally correct for `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack/input.cs` and broadly aligned with likely user expectations for an `ImmutableStack<IItem>` using `PolymorphicMode.IndividualTypeIds`. The generated code preserves stack enumeration order by reading into a staging collection and reconstructing with `ImmutableStack.CreateRange(Reverse(...))`, which matches the generator's explicit `ImmutableStack` special case in `src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/Core/CollectionUtilities.cs:103-113`. No material correctness findings found.

## Findings
1. Low: Both serialize paths traverse `Items` redundantly. Each path does a full pre-validation pass, then a separate LINQ `Count()` pass, then the actual write loop, even though the later `switch` already contains `case null` / `default` guards. For `ImmutableStack<T>`, `Count()` is not backed by a count property, so this is another enumeration rather than an O(1) lookup (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:134-177`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:193-236`, `src/FourSer.Gen/TypeInfoProvider.cs:545-557`).
2. Low: The source member is non-nullable, but the generated serializer still accepts `null` and canonicalizes it to an empty stack on the wire. `input.cs` declares `ImmutableStack<IItem> Items` without `?`, yet the serializer writes count `0` for `null` and deserialization always reconstructs a non-null `ImmutableStack<IItem>` (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack/input.cs:8-12`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:83-84`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:123-124`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:144-147`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:203-206`). This is consistent with current generator metadata (`src/FourSer.Gen/TypeInfoProvider.cs:545-557`) but may still surprise users reading the source model.
3. Info: The generated output contains avoidable redundancy. The `case null` arms in both serializer `switch` statements are dead immediately after the upfront null-validation loops, the same polymorphic type map is re-emitted across sizing, both deserializers, and both serializers, and the three empty leaf serializers repeat near-identical boilerplate (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:38`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:61-79`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:101-119`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:153-176`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:212-235`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:243-462`).

## Performance opportunities
- If the generator keeps this collection shape allocation-free, the serializer should still avoid the current three-pass pattern over `ImmutableStack<T>`. A single staging/materialization pass or a combined validation-and-count pass would remove redundant traversal before writing (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:134-177`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:193-236`).
- The stream serializer currently performs one `StreamWriter.WriteByte` call per item discriminator. In this fixture the leaf serializers are empty, so the payload after the count is just discriminator bytes; batching those bytes into a span and using `StreamWriter.WriteBytes` would reduce stream call count for large collections (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:209-229`, `src/FourSer.Gen/Resources/Code/StreamWriterHelpers.cs:15-17`, `src/FourSer.Gen/Resources/Code/StreamWriterHelpers.cs:33-36`).
- Deserialization currently uses `List<IItem>` plus `Enumerable.Reverse(...)` before `ImmutableStack.CreateRange(...)`. Because the count is known up front, a pre-sized array filled from the end could remove the extra reverse iterator layer while preserving observable stack order (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:55-84`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack/PolymorphicCollectionImmutableStack.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:95-124`, `src/FourSer.Gen/CodeGenerators/Core/CollectionUtilities.cs:108-110`).

## Open questions / assumptions
- Assuming the current contract intentionally treats `null` and empty immutable collections the same on the wire, the generated null-handling is acceptable even though the source member is non-nullable.
- Assuming expected `ImmutableStack<T>` behavior is preservation of observable enumeration order rather than preserving internal node identity, this case is correct. The repo's parity tests clearly expect immutable polymorphic stacks to round-trip as sequences (`tests/FourSer.Tests.Behavioural/Polymorphism/PolymorphicCollectionParityTests.cs:217-271`).
- A targeted local `dotnet test` run could not execute because this machine is missing `Microsoft.NETCore.App 9.0.0`. The verdict is therefore based on static inspection plus a direct runtime sanity check of `ImmutableStack<T>` enumeration and `CreateRange(Reverse(...))` semantics, not on a completed local test run.

# PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode Review

Source: https://github.com/jkamsker/fourser.gen/blob/main/docs/tasks/review-output/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.md

# PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode Review

## Verdict
Mostly correct for the generator's current internal model: `TypeIdProperty` implicitly selects `SingleTypeId`, and the snapshot round-trips its own wire format by reading `TypeId` first and then deserializing a homogeneous `Items` collection from that discriminator (`src/FourSer.Gen/TypeInfoProvider.cs:1276-1282`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:66-107`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:116-157`). It does not fully match likely user expectations, though, because the generated serializer treats `Inventory.TypeId` as a derived output from `Items` rather than an input to serialization.

## Findings
1. Medium: The generated serializer ignores `Inventory.TypeId` as the source of truth and derives the serialized discriminator from `Items` instead. `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/input.cs:10-16` declares a separate `TypeId` member and points the collection at it with `[SerializeCollection(TypeIdProperty = nameof(TypeId))]`. The public contract also describes `TypeIdProperty` as the property that "holds the TypeId for all elements in the collection" and shows it as what "determines the type for all entities" (`src/FourSer.Contracts/SerializeCollectionAttribute.cs:36-39`, `README.md:287-292`); the implementation guide likewise says `SingleTypeId` serialization should read the type id from that property and write it once (`docs/polymorphic_collections_implementation_guide.md:163-167`). In the snapshot, however, both serializers ignore `obj.TypeId`: they write `10` for empty or `null` collections (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:200-203`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:311-314`) and otherwise recompute the discriminator from `obj.Items[0]` (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:206-215`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:317-326`). That means `TypeId = 20` with an empty list still serializes as `10`, and a mismatched `TypeId` is silently ignored rather than validated.
2. Low: The non-nullable `Items` member is treated as optional and normalized on deserialize. `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/input.cs:16` declares `List<Item> Items` without `?`, but the serializers accept `null`, emit the same wire shape as an empty list (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:200-203`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:217-220`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:311-314`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:328-331`), and deserialize back to a non-null `List<Item>` every time (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:69-75`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:119-125`). That is internally consistent, but it is still a likely surprise from the source model.
3. Info: The snapshot contains a fair amount of redundant generated code. The same collection validation and discriminator resolution logic is emitted in both serializers and then recomputed again for the actual write/switch (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:167-198`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:206-234`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:278-309`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:317-345`). The concatenated output also repeats identical `using` blocks and nearly identical zero-member serializers for `Item`, `Sword`, `Shield`, and `Potion` (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:380-673`).

## Performance opportunities
- No meaningful stream batching win exists in this exact snapshot because `Sword`, `Shield`, and `Potion` serialize no payload bytes; the stream path already performs only the scalar `TypeId` and count writes for `Inventory`, and the per-item loops are effectively CPU-only (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:313-330`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:349-368`).
- Reuse the first-pass `validatedDiscriminator` for the actual `TypeId` write and collection switch instead of recomputing it from `obj.Items[0]` twice in each serializer (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:174-196`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:206-234`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:285-307`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:317-345`).
- `GetPacketSize` performs another full discriminator-validation pass over the same list, so sizing plus serialization currently re-walks the collection multiple times (`tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:30-51`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:167-198`, `tests/FourSer.Tests/GeneratorTestCases/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode/PolymorphicCollectionImplicitMode.RunGeneratorTest.verified.txt:278-309`).

## Open questions / assumptions
- This review assumes the attribute/docs wording is the intended contract for `TypeIdProperty`. If the intended behavior is instead "derive the discriminator from the collection and only surface it through the property on deserialize", then the first finding is primarily a documentation and expectation mismatch rather than a serializer defect.
- Static review only. I did not run generator or behavioral tests because the task was limited to producing the report without making other code changes.
